notes: READ THIS FIRST. (1) Grades used here, adapted from SCHEMA.md for benchmark evidence: A = primary artefact read directly by us (the evaluator's own results file / API record / paper table / LICENSE file); B = dated press about a result (none used); C = vendor or author documentation, model card or self-reported claim; D = third-party aggregator, tracker or informal community comparison; E = our own estimate (none used). Where a result is our own arithmetic on a primary table it is graded A and says so. (2) 'Frontier model best in Hebrew?' There is NO published Hebrew text-quality head-to-head of current GPT / Claude / Gemini API models that we could find: the DICTA+MAFAT board is open-weights only and was archived on 2026-05-15; Anthropic's multilingual table, OpenAI's MMMLU and Global-MMLU-Lite (Google/Cohere) all omit Hebrew; arena.ai has no language filter. The closest frontier-vs-frontier Hebrew evidence is per modality: handwriting OCR (ivrit.ai, 2026-09-04), TTS (ivrit.ai TTS Arena Hebrew) and STT (ivrit.ai leaderboard). (3) Model and product names (Gemini 4 Carbon, Claude Opus 5.5 / Fable 5.1, GPT-6 Astra, Muse Wonder, Kimi K3, GLM-5.3, MiMo-V2.6-Pro, gpt-5.6-sol ...) are copied exactly as printed by the sources on 2026-11-05; we did not cross-check them against vendor announcements. (4) Dates: a leaderboard that shows no date has source_date null and the note says what date we used instead. Hub 'lastModified' is used only when stated in the note. (5) URL policy: where we only read a Hugging Face API record (not the HTML page) the row's `url` is the canonical Hub page of that repo and the API URL is in `sources`; vendor home pages we never saw are null. (6) Search limits: the shared web-search budget ran out mid-task, so the last checks (ABBYY, Verbit, Hebrew invoice benchmarks on the open web, Global-MMLU per-language Hebrew rows, Artificial Analysis multilingual coverage) were done only through direct page/API fetches or not at all. See `rejected`. (7) DOUBTS worth a human look: (a) the Hebrew LLM Leaderboard is few-shot, base-model-oriented, has tiny sets (SNLI-he 210, Trivia 300) and visibly mis-scores some chat models (gemma-3-27b-it 13.41, command-a 30.41) - do not present it as a ranking of chat models; (b) licence conflicts: DictaLM-3.0-Nemotron-12B is under the NVIDIA Open Model License although the leaderboard column says apache-2.0; the NeoDictaBERT paper says CC BY-SA while the Hub card says CC BY 4.0; the arXiv page's CC BY-SA belongs to the paper not the DictaLM weights; (c) DictaLM-4.0-105B-A10B-Base appears on the board but has no public page - UNVERIFIED; (d) ivrit.ai runs the STT, TTS and handwriting boards and also trains models that appear on the STT board (conflict of interest); the handwriting set is 225 lines from 10 writers; the TTS arena has ~160-210 votes per main model and its Models page shows different Elo values than its leaderboard view; (e) the Google STT row on the ivrit.ai board does not say which Google model; (f) Artificial Analysis shows no date on either page; arena.ai marks #1 and #10 as Preliminary; (g) licence-sensitive items for a Hebrew business: Mistral Large 2407 (research licence), Cohere Command R+/Aya and Caspi-1.7B and MMS-TTS (CC BY-NC), SASpeech / ILSpeech / Phonikud and therefore Piper's Hebrew voice (non-commercial), CHURRO (Qwen research), Surya weights ($5M cap), n8n (Sustainable Use, not OSI), Open WebUI (branding clause above 50 users), Dify (no multi-tenant without licence), Flowise (archived 2026-08-13, end of life 2026-08-31), Piper (archived; successor GPL-3.0), ivrit.ai datasets (AI training or academic research only). (8) Corrections to common assumptions: Amazon Textract's FAQ lists Hebrew for printed text; Piper's official voices repo does have a Hebrew voice; Azure's Read model reads printed Hebrew but not Hebrew handwriting.
